product.name: Lucy
product.tagline: The shared skill store for Bending Spoons sellers.

skills.name: call-needs-assessment
skills.title: Call Needs Assessment
skills.summary: After a call, pulls the transcript and maps every stated need against what you actually sell. Marks each one solved, partial, gap, or needs validation. Flags commercial and competitive risk.
skills.why: Stops you promising things the product does not do.
skills.description: Post-call needs assessment. Use after any prospect or customer call when the seller says "assess my call", "run a needs assessment", "does our product solve what they asked for", or names a meeting transcript to analyze. Pulls the transcript (Granola, Gong, or pasted notes), extracts stated needs verbatim, maps each to the seller's product honestly (solved / partial / gap / needs validation), flags commercial and competitive risks, and produces the follow-up plan.
sections: Step 4 — Map needs to the product, one row per stated need
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: followup-noshow
skills.title: Follow-ups and No-shows
skills.summary: Nudges holds nobody has accepted, confirms today's meetings, and rebooks anyone who missed one. Never sends a naked reminder.
skills.why: A no-show is not a no.
skills.description: Follow-ups for pending calendar holds and recovery of no-shows. Use for "follow up on pending invites", "confirm today's meetings", morning-of confirms, mid-life nudges on 2-3 day old holds, and rebooking anyone who missed a meeting. Never for declines (objection-handler) or 3+ silent touches (nurture).
sections: No-show recovery (they accepted, then didn't join)
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: human-messaging
skills.title: Human Messaging
skills.summary: Writes the actual emails. Enforces a banned-phrase list and the one-question rule. Grounded in Gap Selling, Sandler, and Josh Braun rather than generic sales copy.
skills.why: Run before drafting anything a prospect will read.
skills.description: How every prospect-facing email gets written. Use before drafting ANY cover, follow-up, rebook, or reply. Grounded in Gap Selling, Sandler, and Josh Braun's prospecting principles. Enforces the banned-phrase list and the one-question rule.
sections: The checklist every draft must pass
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: lucy-publish
skills.title: Publish
skills.summary: Takes a skill you built, adds it to the store, packages it, and drafts the announcement. Refuses to publish anything containing contact data.
skills.why: If you built something good, this is how everyone else gets it.
skills.description: Publish a skill to the Lucy store so every other seller can install it. Use when the seller says "publish this skill", "share this with the team", "add this to Lucy", "put this in the store", or when lucy-sync has found a local-only skill worth sharing. Also use to push an improved version of a skill that already exists in the store.
sections: Step 0: the data check, before anything else
Step 1: understand what is being published
Step 3: put it in the store
Step 5: tell the author what happens next
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: lucy-report
skills.title: Report Card
skills.summary: Counts your meetings booked and opps piped, works out which skills you were running, and sends the numbers back to the store as aggregates. Never sends your name or any prospect's.
skills.why: This is what lets the store rank skills on real outcomes instead of vibes.
skills.description: Send this seller's outcome numbers back to the Lucy store so skills can be ranked on real results. Use when the seller says "send my report", "report my numbers", "lucy report card", "how did my week go", or on the weekly schedule. Counts meetings booked and opportunities piped, attributes them to the skills that were running, and reports aggregates only, never names.
sections: Attribution: which skills get the credit
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: lucy-sync
skills.title: Sync
skills.summary: Pulls the newest version of everything from the store and installs it. Tells you what changed and what you had edited locally before it touches anything.
skills.why: Say "sync lucy" whenever you want to be current.
skills.description: Pull the newest skills from the Lucy store and install them. Use when the seller says "sync lucy", "update lucy", "am I on the latest", "what version am I running", "did anyone publish anything new", or when any other Lucy skill reports a version mismatch. Also use on first run after install to register the machine.
sections: Step 2: work out what this machine is actually running
Step 3: report before you touch anything
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: objection-handler
skills.title: Objection Handler
skills.summary: For when they say no. Researches the prospect's actual stack first, finds the real gap, then replies in a way that teaches something instead of begging for the meeting back.
skills.why: A decline is usually timing, not a no.
skills.description: Use whenever a prospect replies with an objection or declines - "we're covered", "we have a vendor", "not interested", "not the right time", "too expensive", "we build in-house", or objects to receiving a calendar invite. Researches before writing. Never begs for the meeting back.
sections: The reply formula (one reply per decline, maximum)
Process objections (they objected to getting a calendar invite)
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: prospecting-engine
skills.title: Prospecting Engine
skills.summary: The daily motion. Screens accounts, stages a batch, drafts the outreach, logs every outcome. Runs a different sequence depending on whether you are a BDR, AE, or CSM.
skills.why: This is the part that books meetings.
skills.description: The core outbound engine, role-aware. Use whenever the seller says "stage a batch", "run a wave", "who should we contact next", "fire the invites", "morning sweep", "pulse", or "EOD clear". Reads the seller's role from SELLER-CONFIG.md and runs the matching sequence - BDR invite-first, AE email-first, or CSM relationship-first - end to end: screening, drafting, holds, outcome logging.
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: prospecting-onboarding
skills.title: Onboarding
skills.summary: Sets Lucy up for you in about 20 minutes. Interviews you, writes your config, checks your connectors, builds your contact repository, and stages your first batch.
skills.why: Start here. Everything else assumes this has run.
skills.description: Guided first-time setup for the BSP Prospecting Kit. Use when a new seller says "onboard me", "set up prospecting", "get me started", "set up the kit", or opens this kit for the first time with an unfilled SELLER-CONFIG.md. Interviews the seller, writes their config, checks connectors, builds their repository, sets up scheduled tasks, and runs a supervised test drive. Target: first staged batch within 20 minutes.
sections: Step 5 — Rules of the territory (3 minutes)
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun

skills.name: warm-opener
skills.title: Warm Opener
skills.summary: Researches a prospect's public interests and location so the message opens with something real, a result, a local event, something they posted, before the business bit.
skills.why: Warmth is the single biggest lift in the field data so far.
skills.description: Research a prospect's public interests and location to open outreach with a genuinely warm, human subject (sports moment, local event, something they posted) before the business intro. Use when staging covers, drafting follow-ups, or whenever the seller asks to "warm up" a message. Works WITH the human-messaging skill, never instead of it.
sections: Source hierarchy (only use tiers 1-3; tier 4 is banned)
The five gates (all must pass or drop the warm open entirely)
skills.author: Kenny Fasehun
